text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Saturday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- "Arabs must get their house in order," Sheikh Issa of Bahrain tells al-Dustour in an interview. "King Hussein is a dear and much loved brother and we respect his positions."

- Prime Minister Kabariti and Russian Foreign Minister Primakov discuss latest Middle East developments. King Hussein calls Egyptian President Mubarak to follow up issues from their Sharm el-Sheikh summit.

- Planned maintenance of King Abdullah canal should save 10 percent of its water, or 10 million cubic metres. Water Ministry sources say British company will carry out the 10 million dinar ($14.2 million) project.
- Government to propose establishment of agricultural bank to replace debt ridden agricultural credit agency.

- Management of Feisali soccer club call for general meeting on November 21 to discuss a freeze on its sporting activities. The club, whose supporters were involved in a riot two weeks ago against rival fans, also faces financial problems.
- Crown Prince Hassan returns after talks with Bosnian, Croatian leaders.
